 Medicare Part A and B Premiums 2027: New Rates and Deductibles
 BEINSURE 
 Health Insurance --> 
 Health Insurance 
 Nataly Kramer 
 Nov 18, 2026 
 6 min 
 Benefit Health Insurance 
 Health insurance coverage 
 Health Insurance Inclusion 
 Health Insurance Industry 
 Health insurance policy 
 Healthcare Ecosystem 
 Healthcare Sector 
 Medicare Part A premiums and hospital deductibles for 2027 
 Medicare Part B premiums will offset part of the 2027 Social Security COLA 
 Medicare Part B premiums by income in 2027 
 Medicare Part B deductible increases to $292 in 2027 
 Medicare Part D income-related surcharges for 2027 
 Medicare open enrollment ends December 7 
 The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has announced that the standard Medicare Part B premium will increase by 3.2% in 2027, raising monthly costs for millions of Americans covered by the federal health insurance program.
 The standard monthly premium will rise from $202.90 in 2026 to $209.40 in 2027, an increase of $6.50. The annual Part B deductible will also increase by $9, from $283 to $292.
 CMS announced the updated Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles and coinsurance amounts on November 17, 2026, alongside new income-related surcharges for Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage. The agency attributed the higher Part B premium and deductible primarily to projected increases in healthcare spending.
 Key highlights
 The standard Medicare Part B premium will increase by $6.50 to $209.40 per month in 2027, while the annual deductible rises to $292.
 Higher-income beneficiaries will pay monthly Part B premiums of up to $711.80, based primarily on their 2025 income.
 Medicare Part A hospital deductibles will reach $1,776, while Social Security benefits will increase 3.6% under the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment.
 More than 70 mn Americans are enrolled in Medicare , which provides health insurance for people aged 65 and older and certain younger individuals with disabilities or qualifying medical conditions. Approximately 64 mn have both Medicare Part A, which covers hospital care, and Part B, which covers physician services, outpatient treatment and other medical expenses.
 Medicare Part A premiums and hospital deductibles for 2027
 Medicare Part A covers inpatient hospital care, skilled nursing facilities, hospice, inpatient rehabilitation and certain home healthcare services.
 Approximately 99% of Medicare beneficiaries pay no monthly Part A premium because they or their spouses have accumulated sufficient Medicare-covered employment credits.
 For individuals who must purchase Part A coverage, the full monthly premium will increase from $565 in 2026 to $597 in 2027.
 A reduced premium applies to certain individuals with at least 30 quarters of Medicare-covered employment , or qualifying coverage through a spouse. That amount will rise from $311 to $328 per month.
 The inpatient hospital deductible will increase by $40, from $1,736 to $1,776. Unlike the annual Part B deductible, the Part A hospital deductible applies to each benefit period rather than a calendar year.
 It covers the beneficiary’s share of costs for the first 60 days of Medicare-covered inpatient hospital treatment during a benefit period.
 Additional coinsurance charges apply to longer hospital stays and extended care in skilled nursing facilities.
 Medicare Part A cost sharing 2026 2027 
 Inpatient hospital deductible $1,736 $1,776 
 Daily hospital coinsurance, days 61-90 $434 $444 
 Daily hospital coinsurance, lifetime reserve days $868 $888 
 Skilled nursing facility coinsurance, days 21-100 $217 $222 
 Reduced monthly Part A premium $311 $328 
 Full monthly Part A premium $565 $597 
 Source: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
 For hospital stays lasting 61-90 days, beneficiaries will pay $444 per day in 2027.
 The charge rises to $888 per day when using lifetime reserve days, which provide up to 60 additional covered hospital days over a beneficiary’s lifetime. After those reserve days have been exhausted, patients generally become responsible for the full cost of additional inpatient hospital care.
 For extended skilled nursing facility care, daily coinsurance for days 21-100 will increase to $222, compared with $217 in 2026.
 Beneficiaries with traditional Medicare may have some of these expenses covered through Medicare Supplement Insurance, commonly known as Medigap. Medicare Advantage plans generally establish their own hospital cost-sharing arrangements.
 Medicare Part B premiums will offset part of the 2027 Social Security COLA
 The higher Medicare Part B premium will reduce part of the increase in Social Security payments scheduled for January 2027.
 The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) on October 14, which is expected to increase the average retired worker’s monthly benefit by approximately $75.
 For beneficiaries paying the standard Part B premium through automatic deductions from Social Security, the additional $6.50 monthly Medicare charge will reduce that average increase to approximately $68.50, before any other deductions or adjustments.
 The Part B increase is considerably smaller than the $17.90 monthly premium increase implemented for 2026, which was the second-largest dollar increase in the program’s history.
 Unlike Social Security’s COLA , Medicare Part B premiums are not adjusted through a direct inflation formula. Under the Social Security Act, standard beneficiary premiums are generally designed to finance approximately 25% of projected Part B costs for beneficiaries aged 65 and older.
 Most Medicare beneficiaries who receive Social Security have their Part B premiums deducted automatically from monthly benefit payments (see Social Security faces 2032 benefit cuts, but tax reforms could delay them until 2059 ). Individuals who have not yet claimed Social Security, including those delaying retirement benefits until age 67 or later, may receive bills directly from Medicare.
 Medicare Part B premiums by income in 2027
 Most Medicare Part B beneficiaries pay the standard monthly premium of $209.40. Higher-income enrollees must pay additional charges through the income-related monthly adjustment amount (IRMAA).
 CMS estimates that approximately 9% of Part B beneficiaries are subject to income-related premiums.
 For 2027, these surcharges are generally calculated using modified adjusted gross income reported on 2025 federal income tax returns.
 The standard premium applies to individuals with annual income of $112,000 or less and married couples filing jointly with income of $224,000 or less.
 The first income-related surcharge increases monthly premiums to $293.10. At the highest income tier, beneficiaries pay $711.80 per month for full Part B coverage.
 The complete premium schedule for individual and joint tax filers is as follows:
 Individual income Joint income Monthly Part B premium 
 $112,000 or less $224,000 or less $209.40 
 Over $112,000 to $141,000 Over $224,000 to $282,000 $293.10 
 Over $141,000 to $177,000 Over $282,000 to $354,000 $418.80 
 Over $177,000 to $212,000 Over $354,000 to $424,000 $544.40 
 Over $212,000 to under $500,000 Over $424,000 to under $750,000 $670.00 
 $500,000 or more $750,000 or more $711.80 
 Source: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
 For married beneficiaries who lived with their spouse during the tax year but file separate returns, the premium schedule differs.
 Those with income of $112,000 or less pay $209.40 per month. Individuals with income above $112,000 but below $388,000 pay $670, while those earning $388,000 or more pay $711.80.
 Beneficiaries whose income has decreased because of a qualifying life-changing event, such as retirement, divorce or the death of a spouse, may request a reassessment of their IRMAA determination using more recent financial information.
 Some lower-income beneficiaries can receive assistance with Part B premiums through Medicaid or state-administered Medicare Savings Programs.
 Medicare Part B deductible increases to $292 in 2027
 The annual Medicare Part B deductible will increase from $283 in 2026 to $292 in 2027.
 Part B covers physician services, outpatient hospital care, certain home healthcare services, durable medical equipment and other medical services not covered by Part A.
 After meeting the annual deductible, beneficiaries generally pay 20% of Medicare-approved costs for covered services, while Medicare pays the remaining 80%.
 The standard Part B premium generally applies whether a beneficiary uses traditional Medicare or a privately administered Medicare Advantage plan, although plan-specific arrangements may affect individual costs.
 CMS also announced updated premiums for beneficiaries who qualify for Medicare coverage of immunosuppressive drugs following a kidney transplant.
 Since 2023, certain individuals whose full Medicare coverage ends 36 months after a kidney transplant have been eligible to continue Part B coverage specifically for immunosuppressive medications if they do not have qualifying alternative insurance.
 The standard premium for this limited coverage will be $125.70 per month in 2027.
 Income-related adjustments apply to eligible beneficiaries with higher earnings. Monthly charges range from $125.70 to $628.10, depending on income and filing status.
 Medicare Part D income-related surcharges for 2027
 CMS also published the 2027 income-related monthly adjustment amounts for Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage.
 Approximately 9% of Part D beneficiaries pay an income-related surcharge in addition to the monthly premium charged by their prescription drug plan.
 Unlike Part B, Part D does not have a single standard premium. Monthly premiums vary among private insurance plans, and the IRMAA surcharge is added to the applicable plan premium.
 For 2027, the monthly Part D adjustment ranges from $15.40 to $96.40 for beneficiaries whose income exceeds the standard thresholds.
 Individual income Joint income Monthly Part D surcharge 
 $112,000 or less $224,000 or less $0.00 
 Over $112,000 to $141,000 Over $224,000 to $282,000 $15.40 
 Over $141,000 to $177,000 Over $282,000 to $354,000 $39.70 
 Over $177,000 to $212,000 Over $354,000 to $424,000 $64.00 
 Over $212,000 to under $500,000 Over $424,000 to under $750,000 $88.30 
 $500,000 or more $750,000 or more $96.40 
 Source: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
 For married beneficiaries filing separately who lived with their spouse during the tax year, income-related Part D charges are $88.30 per month for income above $112,000 but below $388,000, and $96.40 for income of $388,000 or more.
 Part D income-related adjustments are deducted from Social Security payments or paid directly to Medicare, regardless of how beneficiaries pay their prescription drug plan premiums.
 CMS said approximately two-thirds of Part D beneficiaries pay premiums directly to their plans, while the remainder have premiums deducted from Social Security benefits.
 Medicare open enrollment ends December 7
 The announcement of 2027 Medicare premiums comes during the annual open enrollment period, which runs from October 15 through December 7, 2026. During this period, eligible beneficiaries can review their existing Medicare coverage and make changes for the following year.
 Available options include switching Medicare Advantage plans, changing standalone Part D prescription drug coverage or moving between traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage, subject to applicable enrollment rules.
 The updated Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles and coinsurance amounts will take effect in January 2027.
 For beneficiaries receiving Social Security, the new Part B premium will generally be reflected in the monthly benefit payment alongside the 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment.
